page.title: Scenario Explorer
page.purpose: Let an author see one scenario's entire declared experience — pages by state, depth, and coverage gaps — and judge what is missing.

priorities.statement: The pages-by-state grid with depth badges is the first thing read.
Coverage gaps (unspecced routes, missing required states) are explicit, not inferable.
Every claim shows its enforcement tier honestly wherever it appears.

states.description: Scenario has a spec; grid, gaps, and claims render.
Scenario has no experience/ folder; the explorer routes the author to the Studio instead of dead-ending.
Some spec files are unreadable/invalid; readable pages render, broken ones are named with their parse error.

regions.purpose: Render the selected scenario's loading, ready, empty, partial, or failed specification surface.

elements.name: Pages by state
elements.description: Rows = pages, columns = states, cells = claim coverage; L0–L4 badge per row.

elements.name: Coverage gaps
elements.description: Routes without specs and declared-state gaps vs the DESIGN.md state contract.

elements.name: Claims
elements.description: All claims of the selected page with tier and latest verdict.
Textual tier tag (machine / manual / aspirational) on every claim row.
Per-claim link to the Evidence view.

claims.statement: The pages-by-state grid is exposed as a real table with its accessible name.
Coverage gaps are visible without scrolling on desktop — missing intent is never below the fold.
Every claim row carries a textual tier label — tier is never conveyed by color alone.
claims.rationale: BAS v1 AX joins do not reliably expose this repeated per-claim text node as default-state evidence; keep manual until the row-level tier traversal is mechanically checked.

claims.statement: Each claim's evidence link is keyboard reachable from the claim list.
claims.rationale: BAS v1 AX joins do not reliably expose this repeated per-claim link as default-state evidence; keep manual until the evidence-link traversal is mechanically checked.

claims.statement: Open-in-Studio is keyboard reachable, so exploring flows directly into authoring.
The no-spec state renders dedicated guidance that routes the author to the Studio.
claims.rationale: v1 BAS reconciliation captures only the default state; this empty-state promise needs multi-state capture before it can be machine tier.

claims.statement: When some spec files are invalid, the explorer names each broken file with its parse error instead of hiding or failing the whole scenario.
claims.rationale: Requires seeded broken fixtures to check mechanically; promotion candidate.
